To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

‐ the social responsibility of companies is a concept that has become central in their communication, but that they do not really know how to express it, and that they are not able to define the meaning of this term in their communication ‐ in their communication, the social responsibility of the company is a concept that is used to justify the existence of companies, and to justify the legitimacy of the economic system in which they operate.

the companies’ social responsibility discourse can be divided into two main categories: a first one, which is based on a metaphorical structure of the social role of the company as an institution and a second, which is based a metaphorical structure that sees the company as an organism.

1) The social responsibility of the company is a subject which is increasingly present in the institutional discourse of companies; 2) The companies are aware of the fact that they are responsible for the social environment in which they operate; 3) The companies have developed a social responsibility policy which is not limited to the field of social responsibility but is extended to all aspects of corporate governance and to the entire organization; 4) The companies are concerned about the social responsibility of their shareholders and their stakeholders
In summary, our research is concerned with
the analysis of the discourses on social responsibility of four large French companies.
the rhetoric of social and environmental responsibility in France.
the rhetoric of corporate social responsibility, and more particularly with the way in which companies present themselves as socially responsible.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
social responsibility is not only a question of communication, but also a question of relationship and of the relationship to oneself, to the others and to the world.
the corporate world, through the use of a wide variety of semantic tools, is able to reveal its true perception of the role of the company in the field of social responsibility.
social responsibility is not a simple matter of social and economic performance but a question of ethics and morality.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the companies do not say what they do, but what they want the public to believe they do.
the social responsibility of a company is not an end in itself but an opportunity to improve the company’s image and to increase the company’s profits.
the social responsibility for the companies is a matter of communication.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, despite their rhetoric of social responsibility, companies are still very far from the implementation of a true social responsibility.
the rhetoric used by the companies in their institutional communications reveals the social responsibility that they attribute to themselves, and the way they conceive their role in society.
the social role that is assigned to the company in the four communications is that of the “good citizen”, which is the metaphor that we have identified as the most frequent.
